edits.old: **Configuration.** `CURE_PERIOD_DAYS` and `restructure.max_breaks` are parameter values in force, loaded and approved through rwb-decision and rwb-case; the design example reads 30 calendar days for MORTGAGE and `restructure.max_breaks = 2` (ASM-4488). edits.new: **Configuration.** `CURE_PERIOD_DAYS` and `restructure.max_breaks` are parameter values in force, loaded and approved through rwb-decision and rwb-case; the design example reads 30 calendar days for MORTGAGE and `restructure.max_breaks = 2` (ASM-4488). The package code of the RES rule set is not published by any source (GAP-2706); the RES rule set is evaluated in rwb-treatment with the package in force from rwb-decision, and no plan event is published in wave 2 (GAP-2706). The tolerance and window values of the match stay with rwb-payment and are not read by this slice (GAP-1628). The match consequence is read through the read in RWB-P8-E2027-CON, returning for a case, plan and business date the payment code, installment due date, match type, rule ID, package code and version and shortfall (GAP-2705). The plan states on the treatment state column are PLAN_RUNNING, PLAN_CURE_PERIOD, PLAN_BROKEN and BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION; a breach writes outcome BROKEN and sets outcome_at, and the local decision record stamps the rule ID and package version (GAP-1880; GAP-2705). The breach decision code is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1880). rwb-treatment publishes rwb.treatment.TreatmentClosed.v1 once for a breached plan; completed-plan closure stays with the plan story (GAP-1881). The numeric operations values, including the alert thresholds and the cache and queue limits, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2508); secrets and the workload identity are referenced by role (GAP-2508).
